source.title: On the Implicit Biases of Architecture & Gradient Descent

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Figure 2 results are described qualitatively, but the supplied text gives no exact plotted values.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares interpolating kernel and finite-width neural network classifiers with ensemble classifiers and reports held-out error. It tests a related aspect of V1 using a different method, but does not test fitting random labels.
record.gate_note: The experiments report held-out error for interpolating classifiers on even/odd MNIST and comparisons with Gibbs and Bayes classifiers. No reported experiment fits random training labels or measures the training–test gap directly. Figure 2 values are not stated numerically in the text.
record.test_reason: The paper studies kernel interpolation as an approximation to ensemble majority voting. It does not test any specified version. In particular, natural-label interpolation and generalization alone do not test V1's coexistence of random-label memorization and natural-label generalization in the same architecture and training recipe.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the empirical conclusions, with the qualification that the GP comparison uses isotropic classifiers. The paper also derives PAC-Bayes risk bounds and argues that large-margin infinite-width networks are Bayes point machines; extending this interpretation to finite-width networks remains an experimentally supported suggestion.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments study kernel interpolation and large-margin MLPs against GP and MLP ensemble classifiers on even/odd MNIST. The finite-width networks use the Nero optimizer and squared loss; the paper does not reproduce the random-label experiments or recipes described in V1.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper compares isotropic GP classifiers and kernel interpolation, and separately finite-width MLPs and their ensemble approximations; plotted results vary with the number of training examples.

fits_no_version.finding: On even/odd MNIST, the centroidal kernel interpolator nearly matches the isotropic GP Bayes classifier's test error; both outperform the Gibbs classifier.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Centroidal kernel interpolation can approximate the test performance of an isotropic GP majority-vote classifier.

fits_no_version.finding: A large-margin width-1000, depth-7 ReLU MLP closely matches the approximate Bayes classifier formed from 501 small-margin MLPs, and both outperform the approximate Gibbs classifier.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A finite-width network trained to large margin can approximate its corresponding ensemble majority classifier's test performance.

fits_no_version.finding: The large-margin MLP and its NN–GP equivalent kernel interpolator have closely agreeing test-error learning curves.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large-margin finite-width MLPs can exhibit test performance similar to their corresponding kernel interpolators.

record.problems: The authors state that an extensive investigation across varied datasets and architectures was beyond the paper's scope. The relevant experimental results are presented as plots without numerical values or uncertainty estimates in the supplied text. The finite-width results use one stated dataset and a specific width-1000, depth-7 MLP setup.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results bearing on the tested version were reported in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting capacity, natural-label generalization under the same recipe, and chance-level held-out performance after random-label training.
Test error as width increases beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Qiso randomizes output magnitudes within the orthant fixed by the natural binary labels; it does not randomize class assignments. Exact plotted test errors are unavailable in the supplied text. The corrected row states indicate that these measures cannot establish the specified versions, not that their reported classifier comparisons failed.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test fitting random labels, held-out chance accuracy after random-label fitting, the specified Inception/AlexNet/MLP settings, or standard gradient methods; its finite-width MLP uses the Nero optimizer and a large-margin squared loss.
